title: شہادہ - ایمان کا اعلان

content.starter: شہادہ کہتا ہے: "اللہ کے سوا کوئی معبود نہیں، اور محمد ﷺ اس کے رسول ہیں۔" یہ اسلام میں سب سے اہم جملہ ہے! جب ہم اسے کہتے ہیں، تو ہم سب کو بتاتے ہیں کہ ہم اللہ پر یقین رکھتے ہیں اور اس کے نبی سے محبت کرتے ہیں۔ یہ ہمارے دل کو ہلکا اور خوش کرتا ہے!
content.explorer: شہادہ اسلام کا پہلا ستون ہے۔ اس میں دو حصے ہیں: پہلا، یقین رکھنا کہ صرف اللہ ہی خدا ہے — کوئی اور عبادت کے لائق نہیں۔ دوسرا، یقین رکھنا کہ نبی محمد ﷺ اللہ کے آخری رسول ہیں۔ شہادہ کو صداقت کے ساتھ کہنا آپ کو مسلم بناتا ہے۔ یہ صرف الفاظ نہیں ہیں — بلکہ یہ آپ کے دل سے اللہ کے ہدایت کے پابندی کرنے کا عہد ہے۔
content.thinker: شہادا صرف ایک اعلان سے بہت زیادہ ہے — یہ ایک مکمل دنیاوی نظریہ ہے۔ پہلا حصہ، "لا الٰہ الا اللہ"، تمام جھوٹے معبودوں کو مسترد کرتا ہے اور توحید (توحید) کو تصدیق کرتا ہے۔ دوسرا حصہ، "محمد رسول اللہ"، محمد ﷺ کی نبوی اتھارٹی قائم کرتا ہے۔ دونوں مل کر وہ بنیاد بناتے ہیں جس پر تمام اسلامی عملے قائم ہیں۔ شہادے کو سمجھنا اللہ کی اطاعت کی اصل کو سمجھنا ہے۔

funFact: جانتے تھے؟ شہادہ نئی پیدا ہونے والی بچی کے کان میں اچھنتی ہے اور یہ بہت سے مسلمانوں کی آخری الفاظ بھی ہیں جن کی وہ موت سے پہلے کہنے کا خواہش رکھتے ہیں!

quiz.explanation: شہادہ کا مطلب 'ایمان کا اعلان' ہے — یہ وہ بیان ہے جو کوئی شخص مسلم بناتا ہے۔

quiz.explanation: شہادہ میں دو حصے ہیں: ایک خدا میں یقین رکھنا اور دوسرا محمد ﷺ اس کے رسول ہونے میں یقین رکھنا۔

title: Salah - نماز

content.starter: Salah Allah سے بات کرنا ہے! ہم دن میں پانچ بار کچھ کرنا چھوڑتے ہیں، ہاتھ اور چہرے دھوتے ہیں (اسے wudu کہتے ہیں)، Mecca کی طرف رخ کرتے ہیں، اور نماز پڑھتے ہیں۔ یہ Allah کے ساتھ ایک خاص فون کال ہے۔ وہ جب ہم اس سے بات کرتے ہیں تو بہت خوش ہوتا ہے!
content.explorer: Salah اسلام کا دوسرا ستون ہے۔ مسلمان دن میں پانگ بار نماز پڑھتے ہیں: Fajr (صبح)، Dhuhr (دوپہر)، Asr (شام)، Maghrib (غروب) اور Isha (رات)۔ ہر نماز میں Quran کی آیات پڑھتے ہوئے کھڑے ہونا، گھٹنے گرنا اور سجدہ کرنا شامل ہے۔ Salah ہمیں پورے دن میں Allah سے جوڑے رکھتی ہے اور ہمیں نظم و ضبط اور شکرانہ سکھاتی ہے۔
content.thinker: پانچ روزانہ نمازیں (Salawat) Allah کا تحفہ ہیں، جنہیں Night Journey (Isra and Mi'raj) کے دوران فرمایا گیا تھا۔ ہر نماز ایک روحانی حالت کے مطابق ہے: Fajr دن شروع ہونے سے پہلے روح کو پاک کرتی ہے، Dhuhr دوپہر میں دوبارہ توانائی فراہم کرتی ہے، Asر غور و فکر کی ترغیب دیتی ہے، Maghrib دن کے برکات کے لیے شکرانہ کا اعلان کرتی ہے، اور Isha سونے سے پہلے امن فراہم کرتی ہے۔ جسمانی حرکات — کھڑے ہونا (qiyam)، گھٹنے گرنا (ruku) اور سجدہ کرنا (sujud) — خضرت کے اعمال ہیں جو ہمیں اپنے خالق کے ساتھ تعلقات یاد دلاتے ہیں۔

funFact: جانتے تھے؟ مسلمان جہاں بھی دنیا میں ہوں، نماز پڑھتے وقت Mecca کی طرف رخ کرتے ہیں! خلابازی سے بھی، خلابازوں نے Mecca کی طرف نماز پڑھی!

quiz.explanation: مسلمان دن میں پانچ بار نماز پڑھتے ہیں: Fajr، Dhuhr، Asr، Maghrib، اور Isha۔

quiz.explanation: ہم نماز پڑھنے سے پہلے wudu (ablution) کرتے ہیں تاکہ خود کو صاف رکھ سکیں۔

quiz.explanation: مسلمان Mecca میں Kaaba کی طرف رخ کرتے ہیں، جسے Qibla کہتے ہیں۔

title: زکات - خیرات

content.starter: زکات کا مطلب ہے کہ ہم اپنے پاس ہونے والے چیزوں کو دوسروں کے ساتھ بانٹنا! اگر ہم میں اضافی پیسے ہیں، تو ہم ان لوگوں کو ایک چھوٹا سا حصہ دیتے ہیں جھوٹے ہیں۔ یہ اللہ کی طرف سے ہمارے پرہیزگار اور بانٹنے کی دعوت ہے۔ جب ہم دیتے ہیں، تو ہمارے دلوں کو خوشی ہوتی ہے!
content.explorer: زکات اسلام کا تیسرا ستون ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے ہر سال اپنے بچھڑے ہوئے پیسوں کا 2.5% ضروری افراد کو دینا۔ یہ اختیاری نہیں ہے — یہ ایک فرض ہے مسلمانوں کے لیے جو ایک خاص حد سے زیادہ دولت رکھتے ہیں۔ زکات ہمارے پیسوں کو پاک کرتی ہے اور یاد دلاتی ہے کہ سب کچھ اللہ کا ہے۔ یہ غریبوں کی مدد کرتی ہے، قرضوں کو چھوڑتی ہے، اور برادری کو مضبوط کرتی ہے۔
content.thinker: زکات ایک سماجی اور روحانی فرض ہے۔ لفظ 'زکات' کا مطلب 'پاک کرانا' اور 'بڑھنا' ہے — اپنے دولت کا حصہ دے کر، ہم باقی کو پاک کرتے ہیں اور روحانی طور پر بڑھتے ہیں۔ اللہ قرآن میں فرماتے ہیں کہ جو لوگ زکات دیتے ہیں وہ اپنے آپ کو پاک کر رہے ہیں (التوبہ 9:103)۔ 2.5% (ایک اڑائیسواں) کا مقررہ شرح ایک قمری سال سے زیادہ نسیب حد سے اوپر رکھے گئے بچھڑے ہوئے پیسوں پر لاگو ہوتا ہے۔ دولت کی اس نظاماتیک تقسیم کا تصور انقلابی تھا اور اب بھی اسلام کی طاقتور ترین سماجی انصاف کے آلات میں سے ایک ہے۔

funFact: جانتے تھے؟ لفظ 'زکات' کا مطلب 'پاک کرانا' ہے — جب تم زکات دیتے ہو، تمہارا باقی پیسے مبارک اور پاک ہو جاتا ہے!

quiz.explanation: مسلمان ہر سال اپنے بچھڑے ہوئے پیسوں کا 2.5% (ایک اڑائیسواں) زکات کے طور پر دیتے ہیں۔

quiz.explanation: زکات کا مطلب 'پاک کرانا' ہے — یہ ہمارے دولت اور دلوں کو پاک کرتی ہے۔

quiz.explanation: زکات ضرورت مند لوگوں کو دیا جاتا ہے، غریبوں، قرضداروں اور مسافروں سمیت۔

title: سوم - رمضان میں روزہ

content.starter: رمضان میں، ہم صبح سغری سے غروب تک کھانا یا پینہ نہیں کرتے۔ اسے روزہ کہتے ہیں! یہ ہمیں صبر کرنے سے سکھاتا ہے اور ہمیں اس بات پر سوچنے پر مجبور کرتا ہے کہ جو لوں کے پاس کھانا نہیں ہوتا۔ رات کو، ہم اپنے خاندان کے ساتھ روزہ توڑتے ہیں ا� مل کر نماز پڑھتے ہیں۔ یہ بہت خاص ہے!
content.explorer: سوم کا مطلب ہے رمضان کے مہینے میں روزہ رکھنا، اسلام کا چوتھا ستون۔ صبح سغری سے غروب تک، مسلمان کھانا، پینا اور دوسرے جسمانی ضروریات سے پہرہ کرتے ہیں۔ لیکن روزہ صرف بھوک رہنے کے بارے میں نہیں ہے — یہ صبر بنانے، غریبوں کے لیے ہمدردی پیدا کرنے اور اللہ سے قریب آنے کے بارے میں ہے۔ غروب آفتاب پر روزہ ایفٹر نامی کھانے سے توڑا جاتا ہے، جو اکثر خاندان اور برادری کے ساتھ شیڈ کیا جاتا ہے۔
content.thinker: رمضان میں سوم جسمانی، ذہنی اور روحانی عبادت کا ایک جامع عمل ہے۔ قرآن پہلی بار رمضان میں نازل ہوا (سورہ البقرہ 2:185)، جس سے اس مہینے کو خاص طور پر مقدس بنا دیا گیا۔ روزہ اللہ کے وجود کا جسمانی یاد دہانہ بناتے ہوئے تقوی (خدا سے آگاہی) کو فروغ دیتا ہے۔ کھانے اور پینے سے پہرہ کرنے کے علاوہ، مسلمانوں کو منفی گفتگو، غصب اور غیبت سے بچنے کی ترغیب دی جاتی ہے۔ صبح کا کھانا (سحور) اور غروب کا کھانا (افطار) شکرانہ اور برادری کا ایک رتھ بناتا ہے جو پورے مہینے کو بدل دیتا ہے۔

quiz.explanation: غروب آفتاب پر روزہ توھنے کے لیے کھانا افطار کہلاتا ہے۔

title: حج - مکہ کی زیارت

content.starter: حج مکہ کا ایک بڑا سفر ہے! ہر مسل جو اس کا قابل ہو وہاں اللہ کے گھر کے گرد نماز پڑھنے کے لیے جاتا ہے — کعبہ کے گرد۔ ملینوں لوگ مل کر جاتے ہیں، سادہ سفید کپڑے پہنتے ہوئے۔ وہاں ہر کسی برابر ہے — امیر یا غریب، اس کا کوئی فرق نہیں پڑتا!
content.explorer: Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam — a pilgrimage to Mecca that every Muslim must make at least once in their lifetime if they are able. It happens during the Islamic month of Dhul Hijjah. Pilgrims wear simple white clothes called Ihram, circling the Kaaba, walking between hills, and standing in prayer at Arafat. Hajj teaches equality, patience, and devotion to Allah.
content.thinker: حج دنیا کا سب سے بڑا سالانہ اجتماع ہے اور اسلامی اتحاد کی اعلیٰ ترین اظہار ہے۔ حضرت ابراہیم ﷺ اور ان کے خاندان کے پاؤں کے نقوش پر چلتے ہوئے، زیارت کار ایسے رسوم انجام دیتے ہیں جن کا مطلب قربانی، پاکی، اور اللہ کی اطاعت ہے۔ احرام پہننے سے دولت اور عہدے کی تمام نشانیاں ختم ہو جاتی ہیں — اللہ کے سامنے ہر کسی برابر ک�ڑتا ہے۔ رسول اللہ ﷺ نے فرمایا: 'حج جو شخص اس کا قابل ہو اپنی زندگی میں ایک بار فرض ہے۔' یہ ایک گہرا روحانی سفر ہے جو گناہوں کو صاف کرتا ہے اور خالق کے ساتھ آپ کے رشتے کو تازہ کرتا ہے۔

funFact: جانتے ہوے؟ ہر سال 2 ملین سے زیادہ لوگ حج کرتے ہیں! جب زیارت کار ستونوں (جمارات) پر پتھر مارتے ہیں، تو وہ حضرت ابراہیم ﷺ کی مثال پیچھے چل رہے ہیں!

title: Tawheed - خداوند کا اکھر

content.starter: توحید کا مطلب ہے کہ صرف ایک ہی خدا ہے — اللہ! نے سب کچھ بنایا: تم، میں، ستارے، جانور، سب کچھ! ہم صرف اللہ کی عبادت کرتے ہیں، کسی اور کے لیے نہیں۔ اللہ ہی واحد ہے جسے ہمارا پیار اور عبادت حاصل ہونا چاہیے!
content.explorer: توحید اسلام میں سب سے اہم یقین ہے — کہ صرف ایک خدا ہے، اللہ۔ اس کے شرکا، خاندان اور برابر نہیں ہیں۔ وہ ہر چیز کا خالق ہے اور عبادت کے واحد لائق۔ توحید کو سمجھنا یہ معلوم کرتا ہے کہ ہم مجسموں، لوگوں، یا کسی اور چیز کی عبادت نہیں کرتے — صرف اللہ کی۔ یہ یقین اسلام میں ہر چیز کی بنیاد ہے۔
content.thinker: توحید اسلامی الٰہیات کا سنگ بنیاد ہے، جس میں تین ابعاد شامل ہیں: توحید ربوبیہ (ربوبیت کا اکھر)، توحید الٰہیہ (عبادت کا اکھر)، اور توحید اسماء و صفات (اسماء و صفات کا اکھر)۔ پہلا اللہ کو واحد خالق اور قائم رکھنے والے کے طور پر تسلیم کرتا ہے۔ دوسرا تمام اقسام کی عبادات صرف اس کی طرف ہی موڑتا ہے۔ تیسرا یہ تصدیق کرتا ہے کے اللہ کے صفات منفرد اور قابل موازنہ نہیں ہیں۔ قرآن میں کہا گیا ہے: 'کہو، وہ اللہ ہے، اکھر۔ اللہ، �مستقل پناہ۔ وہ نہیں پالتا اور نہیں پلایا جاتا۔ اور اس کے برابر کوئی نہیں ہے' (سورہ الاخلاص 112:1-4)۔

funFact: جانتے تھے؟ کہ لفظ 'اسلام' 'سلام' سے آتا ہے جس کا مطلب امن ہے، اور اس کا مطلب اللہ کی اطاعت — ایک خدا کی!

title: فرشتے

content.starter: فرشتے روشنی سے بنے ہوئے خاص مخلوقات ہیں! اللہ انہیں ہماری مدد کے لیے بھیجتا ہے۔ کچھ فرشتے ہمارے اچھے اور برے اعمال لکھتے ہیں۔ کچھ فرشتے وقت آجانے پر ہمارے روحوں کو لے جاتے ہیں۔ فرشتے ہمیشہ اللہ کی اطاعت کرتے ہیں اور کبھی غلطی نہیں کرتے!
content.explorer: فرشتے اسلام میں ایمان کے چھوے ارکان میں سے ایک ہیں۔ وہ روشنی سے پیدا کیے گئے ہیں اور ہمیشہ اللہ کی اطاعت کرتے ہیں۔ سب سے مشہور فرشتہ جبریل (گبرییل) ہے، جس نے اللہ کے پیغامات انبیاء تک پہنچائے۔ دیگر اہم فرشتوں میں میکائیل (میکائل)، اسرافیل (جو قیامت کے دن بوق بجائے گا) اور عزرائیل (موت کا فرشتہ) شامل ہیں۔ فرشتے ہمارے اعمال کو ریکارڈ کرتے ہیں اور ہماری حفاظت کرتے ہیں۔
content.thinker: فرشتے (ملائکہ) اسلامی ایمان کا بنیادی جزو ہیں۔ روشنی سے پیدا کیے گئے، وہ مختلف بعد میں موجود ہیں اور مختلف صلاحیتوں میں اللہ کی خدمت کرتے ہیں۔ جبریل (گبرییل) نے قرآن نبی محمد ﷺ تک پہنچایا۔ کرمان کاتبین ریکارڈنگ فرشتے ہیں جو ہر کام کو دستاویز کرتے ہیں۔ فرشتے منکر اور نکر مرگ میں مردے ہوئے سوال کرتے ہیں۔ انسانی مخلوقوں کے برعکس، فرشتے کوئی آزارئہ ارادہ نہیں رکھتے — وہ ہمیشہ اللہ کی اطاعت کرتے ہیں۔ ان کی موجودگی ہمیں یاد دلاتی ہے کہ ہم کبھی واقعی تنہا نہیں ہوتے اور ہمارے اعمال ہمیشہ دیکھے جا رہے ہوتے ہیں۔

funFact: جانتے تھے؟ فرشتے پر ہیں! کچھ کے دو، کچھ کے تین، کچھ کے چار پر ہیں — اور نبی محمد ﷺ نے فرشتہ جبریل کو 600 پروں کے ساتھ دیکھا!

title: Holy Books

content.starter: Allah sent holy books to guide people! The most important one for us is the Quran — Allah's final book, sent to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Before that, Allah sent the Torah to Musa, the Zabur to Dawud, and the Injil to Isa. The Quran is special because Allah promised to protect it!
content.explorer: Muslims believe that Allah revealed several holy books to guide humanity. The Tawrat (Torah) was given to Prophet Musa, the Zabur (Psalms) to Prophet Dawud, and the Injil (Gospel) to Prophet Isa. The Quran is the final and most complete revelation, sent to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. We believe the earlier books were changed over time, but the Quran has been preserved exactly as Allah revealed it.
content.thinker: The belief in holy books (Kutub) is the third article of Islamic faith. Allah revealed guidance through various scriptures: the Sahifat to Ibrahim, the Tawrat to Musa, the Zabur to Dawud, the Injil to Isa, and the Quran to Muhammad ﷺ. While Muslims respect all these revelations, we believe the Quran is the final and preserved word of Allah. It was revealed over 23 years and has been memorized by millions of huffaz (memorizers) throughout history. The Quran is unique in that Allah Himself guaranteed its preservation: 'Indeed, it is We who sent down the Quran and indeed, We will be its guardian' (Surah Al-Hijr 15:9).

funFact: Did you know? The Quran has been completely memorized by millions of people around the world — and some children as young as 7 years old!

quiz.q: Which is the final holy book in Islam?
quiz.explanation: The Quran is the final and most complete holy book sent by Allah.

quiz.q: Which prophet received the Torah?
quiz.explanation: The Torah (Tawrat) was given to Prophet Musa (Moses).

quiz.q: What makes the Quran special?
quiz.explanation: Allah promised to protect the Quran from being changed — it's preserved exactly as revealed.

title: Prophets of Allah

content.starter: Allah sent many prophets to guide people! We believe in 25 prophets, like Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and the last one, Muhammad ﷺ. They were all good people who taught us to worship Allah and be kind to others!
content.explorer: Allah sent prophets to every nation throughout history to guide people to the right path. We know of 25 prophets mentioned in the Quran, including Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad ﷺ. All prophets taught the same message: worship Allah alone and be good to others. Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the last and final prophet.
content.thinker: The belief in prophets (Anbiya) is the fourth article of Islamic faith. Allah sent 124,000 prophets to guide humanity, with 25 specifically mentioned in the Quran. They include the five greatest prophets (Ulul-Azm): Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad ﷺ. Each prophet was sent to a specific nation but carried the same universal message of Tawheed and moral conduct. Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets (Khatam an-Nabiyyin), meaning no new prophet will come after him. His message is for all of humanity until the Day of Judgment.

funFact: Did you know? Muslims believe in 25 prophets mentioned in the Quran! Prophet Nuh (Noah) lived for 950 years and built the big ship!

quiz.q: How many prophets are mentioned in the Quran?
quiz.explanation: 25 prophets are specifically mentioned in the Quran.

quiz.q: Who is the last prophet in Islam?
quiz.explanation: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the last and final prophet sent by Allah.

quiz.q: What did all prophets teach?
options: Worship Allah alone and be kind
quiz.explanation: All prophets taught the same message: worship Allah alone and be good to others.

title: Day of Judgment

content.starter: One day, everyone will come back to life and stand in front of Allah! He will check all our good and bad deeds. People who did good will go to Paradise — a beautiful place with everything nice. People who were bad and didn't sorry will go to Hell. That's why we should always try to do good!
content.explorer: The Day of Judgment (Yawm al-Qiyamah) is when all people will be resurrected and brought before Allah to be judged for their deeds. Every action — even the smallest kindness — will be weighed on a scale. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad will enter Paradise (Jannah), a place of eternal happiness. Those whose bad deeds are heavier will face punishment. This belief motivates Muslims to always do their best.
content.thinker: The Day of Judgment (Qiyamah) is the fifth article of Islamic faith. It is the day when all of creation will be resurrected and judged by Allah with perfect justice. The Prophet ﷺ described signs that will precede it, including major earthquakes, the sun rising from the west, and the emergence of the Dajjal. On that day, every person will receive their book of deeds — in the right hand for the righteous, in the left for the wrongdoers. The scale (Mizan) will weigh every deed, no matter how small. This belief provides moral accountability and motivates Muslims to live righteously.

funFact: Did you know? On the Day of Judgment, even a small good deed — like removing a thorn from the road — will be rewarded!

quiz.q: What happens on the Day of Judgment?
options: Everyone is judged for their deeds
quiz.explanation: On the Day of Judgment, everyone will be judged for their good and bad deeds.

quiz.q: What is the name of Paradise in Arabic?
quiz.explanation: Paradise is called Jannah in Arabic — it means 'garden'.

quiz.q: Will even small deeds be judged?
quiz.explanation: Every deed, no matter how small, will be weighed on the Day of Judgment.

title: Wudu - Ablution

content.starter: Wudu is washing before prayer! We wash our hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head, and feet with clean water. It makes us clean and ready to talk to Allah. Wudu also washes away our small sins — how cool is that!
content.explorer: Wudu is the ritual ablution Muslims perform before praying. It involves washing specific body parts in order: hands, mouth, nose, face, arms to elbows, wiping the head, and washing feet to ankles. Wudu is not just about physical cleanliness — it's also spiritual purification. Each step has benefits: washing the hands removes germs, rinsing the mouth keeps it clean, and washing the feet removes dirt from the road.
content.thinker: Wudu is a beautiful act that combines physical hygiene with spiritual purification. The Quran states: 'Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repenting and loves those who purify themselves' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:222). The Prophet ﷺ said that when a Muslim performs wudu and washes their face, sins fall away with the water. When they wash their hands, sins fall from their hands. When they wash their feet, sins fall from their feet. Wudu is thus both a practical act of cleanliness and a spiritual ritual of renewal.

funFact: Did you know? When you perform wudu and wash each body part, your sins fall away with the water — it's like getting a fresh start!

quiz.q: What do we perform before praying?
quiz.explanation: We perform wudu (ablution) before praying to clean ourselves.

quiz.q: How many steps are in wudu?
quiz.explanation: There are 7 main steps in wudu: hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head, and feet.

quiz.q: What does wudu clean besides the body?
quiz.explanation: Wudu washes away our small sins — it's spiritual purification too!

title: Islamic Dress

content.starter: Allah asks us to dress nicely and modestly! Boys and girls should cover their bodies properly. It's about being respectful and showing that we love Allah. Modest dressing makes us feel confident and proud of being Muslim!
content.explorer: Islamic dress is about modesty and respecting Allah's guidelines. For women, this generally means covering everything except the face, hands, and feet — many choose to wear hijab (headscarf). For men, clothing should cover from the navel to the knees. The key is modesty — not showing off or wearing inappropriate clothes. Islamic dress is an act of worship and identity.
content.thinker: Islamic dress codes are rooted in the Quran and Sunnah. Allah says: 'O Children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid' (Surah Al-A'raf 7:31). The hijab is more than a piece of cloth — it's a statement of identity, dignity, and devotion to Allah. For both men and women, modest dress is about self-respect and not reducing oneself to physical appearance. It's important to understand that modesty is a comprehensive concept that includes behavior, speech, and dress. The goal is to be recognized for one's character and intellect, not merely for appearance.

funFact: Did you know? The word 'hijab' comes from Arabic and means 'curtain' or 'screen' — it's about creating a space of dignity and privacy!

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of Islamic dress?
quiz.explanation: Islamic dress is about modesty and respecting Allah's guidelines.

quiz.q: What does 'hijab' mean?
quiz.explanation: The word 'hijab' means 'curtain' or 'screen' in Arabic.

quiz.q: For men, what part of the body must be covered?
quiz.explanation: Men must cover from the navel to the knees as a minimum.

title: Halal Food

content.starter: Halal means 'okay to eat' in Arabic! Allah tells us what food is good for us. We can eat fruits, vegetables, chicken, and fish. We can't eat pork or drink alcohol. We always say 'Bismillah' before eating to thank Allah!
content.explorer: Halal means permissible in Islam. Allah has told us which foods are halal (allowed) and haram (forbidden). Halal foods include fruits, vegetables, grains, and properly slaughtered meat. Haram foods include pork, blood, alcohol, and meat not slaughtered in Allah's name. Saying 'Bismillah' before eating is a Sunnah and reminds us that food is a blessing from Allah.
content.thinker: The concept of halal and haram in food is rooted in the Quran and Sunnah. Allah says: 'Eat of what is lawful and good on the earth' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:168). Halal is not just about what we eat but how food is obtained — it must be through ethical, humane, and clean methods. Pork is prohibited (haram) as stated in multiple Quranic verses. Alcohol is forbidden because it clouds the mind and leads to sin. Even when eating halal food, Islam teaches moderation: 'Eat and drink, but do not be excessive' (Surah Al-A'raf 31). The act of saying 'Bismillah' before eating transforms a routine meal into an act of worship.

funFact: Did you know? Muslims say 'Bismillah' (In the name of Allah) before eating — it's like saying grace and thanking Allah for the food!

quiz.q: What does 'halal' mean?
quiz.explanation: Halal means 'permissible' — food that Allah allows us to eat.

quiz.q: Which of these is haram (forbidden) in Islam?
quiz.explanation: Pork is haram (forbidden) in Islam.

quiz.q: What do Muslims say before eating?
quiz.explanation: Muslims say 'Bismillah' (In the name of Allah) before eating.

title: Duas - Supplications

content.starter: Duas are prayers we say to Allah anytime! When we wake up, eat, go outside, or feel scared — we can talk to Allah. He always listens! There's a special dua for everything. It's like having a direct line to Allah!
content.explorer: Duas are personal prayers to Allah — conversations where we ask for help, guidance, forgiveness, or express gratitude. Unlike formal salah, duas can be made anytime in any language. The Prophet ﷺ taught us specific duas for waking up, eating, traveling, and more. Making dua shows our dependence on Allah and our trust in His help.
content.thinker: Duas (supplications) represent the direct relationship between a servant and Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Dua is the essence of worship.' Islam teaches duas for every occasion — from waking up ('Alhamdulillahilladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur') to entering the mosque, before sleeping, and during times of distress. Allah says: 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you' (Surah Ghafir 40:60). This is a profound promise — the Creator of the universe invites us to speak with Him directly, without any intermediary.

funFact: Did you know? There's a dua for almost everything — even for when you enter your bathroom! Allah wants us to remember Him in every moment!

quiz.q: What is a dua?
quiz.explanation: A dua is a personal prayer — talking to Allah anytime, anywhere.

quiz.q: Can duas be made in any language?
quiz.explanation: Duas can be made in any language — Allah understands all languages!

quiz.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Dua is the essence of worship.'

title: Reading Quran

content.starter: The Quran is Allah's special book! When we read it, Allah rewards us. Even reading one letter gives us 10 rewards! The Quran teaches us how to be good Muslims and how to live happily. Let's try to read a little bit every day!
content.explorer: The Quran is the holy book of Islam, revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through the angel Jibril. Reading the Quran is one of the most rewarding acts a Muslim can do — each letter earns 10 rewards. Muslims try to read the Quran daily, especially during Ramadan. The Quran is in Arabic, but translations help us understand its meanings. Reading with understanding and reflection is the goal.
content.thinker: The Quran is the literal word of Allah, revealed over 23 years through the angel Jibril to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. It consists of 114 surahs (chapters) and over 6,000 ayahs (verses). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever reads a letter from the Book of Allah will have a reward, and the reward of each letter is multiplied by ten.' Beyond reading, the Quran invites contemplation (tadabbur) — understanding its messages and applying them to life. The Quran is unique in that it has been perfectly preserved in its original Arabic since its revelation, making it the only religious text with an unbroken chain of transmission.

funFact: Did you know? Reading just ONE letter of the Quran earns you 10 rewards from Allah! So reading 'Al-Fatiha' gives you over 1,000 rewards!

quiz.explanation: Angel Jibril (Gabriel) brought the Quran to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

title: How to Pray: A Complete Guide

content.starter:
How do Muslims pray? It starts with Wudu — washing your hands, face, arms, and feet to get clean for Allah. Then you face the Kaaba in Mecca and do special movements: standing, bowing, and putting your forehead on the ground. Each prayer has a name like Fajr (morning) and Maghrib (sunset). There are 5 prayers every day! It's like having 5 special meetings with Allah.

WUDU — The 8 Steps:
1) Niyyah — Make the intention in your heart to perform Wudu for the sake of Allah. 2) Wash Hands — Wash both hands up to the wrists three times, starting with the right hand. Make sure water reaches between your fingers! 3) Rinse Mouth — Take water into your mouth and rinse it thoroughly three times. 4) Rinse Nose — Breathe water in through your nose and blow it out three times. 5) Wash Face — Wash your entire face three times, from forehead to chin and ear to ear. 6) Wash Arms — Wash both arms up to the elbows three times, starting with the right arm. 7) Wipe Head — Wipe your entire head once with wet hands. 8) Wash Feet — Wash both feet up to the ankles three times, starting with the right foot. Make sure water reaches between your toes!

Remember: Take your time with each step, use clean water, and avoid waste. Wudu brings purity to your body and light to your heart!

SALAH — The 7 Main Positions:
1) Niyyah — Intend in your heart to pray. 2) Takbir — Raise your hands to your ears and say 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest). 3) Qiyam — Stand upright with hands crossed at chest level, and recite Surah Al-Fatiha and another Surah. 4) Ruku — Bow forward with your hands on your knees, and say 'Subhana Rabbiyal Azeem' (Glory be to my Lord, the Greatest). 5) Qawmah — Rise from bowing and say 'Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah' (Allah hears those who praise Him). 6) Sujud — Put your forehead, nose, hands, knees, and toes on the ground, and say 'Subhana Rabbiyal A'la' (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High). 7) Tashahhud — Sit and recite the testimony of faith and send blessings upon Prophet Muhammad.

THE 5 DAILY PRAYERS:
- Fajr (Dawn): 2 Fard + 2 Sunnah = 4 rak'ahs — strengthens your faith!
- Dhuhr (Noon): 4 Fard + 6 Sunnah = 10 rak'ahs — find peace and clarity!
- Asr (Afternoon): 4 Fard + 4 Sunnah = 8 rak'ahs — seek Allah's pleasure!
- Maghrib (Sunset): 3 Fard + 2 Sunnah = 5 rak'ahs — build discipline and gratitude!
- Isha (Night): 4 Fard + 2 Sunnah = 6 rak'ahs — connect with your Creator!
Total daily: 17 Fard + 12 Sunnah = 29 rak'ahs combined.
content.explorer:
How to Pray: A Complete Guide covers Wudu (ablution), Salah (prayer), the 5 daily prayers, and the rak'ah breakdown in full detail.

WUDU — The 8 Steps of Ablution:
Wudu is the ritual purification performed before prayer. It is a physical and spiritual cleansing that prepares the body and mind for communication with Allah. Wudu is obligatory before performing Salah and is considered one of the most important prerequisites for prayer. The steps are: 1) Niyyah — make the intention in your heart to perform Wudu for prayer, 2) Wash both hands up to the wrists three times starting with the right hand, ensuring water reaches between fingers, 3) Rinse your mouth thoroughly three times — this cleanses the mouth for recitation, 4) Breathe water in through the nose and blow it out three times using your left hand to assist, 5) Wash your entire face three times from forehead to chin and ear to ear, including the beard if you have one, 6) Wash both arms up to and including the elbows three times starting with the right arm, 7) Wipe your head once with wet hands — you can wipe the entire head or just a portion, 8) Wash both feet up to and including the ankles three times starting with the right foot, ensuring water reaches between the toes.

When is Wudu Required? Before every obligatory prayer (Fard), before voluntary prayers (Sunnah/Nafl), when touching the Quran, and after using the bathroom.

SALAH — The 7 Main Positions of Prayer:
Salah is the Islamic prayer performed five times daily at prescribed times. It is the second pillar of Islam and a direct connection between the believer and Allah. Each prayer consists of one or more rak'ahs (cycles). The seven positions are: 1) Niyyah (Intention) — intend in your heart to pray the specific prayer (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, or Isha). The intention must be clear and sincere. 2) Takbir (Opening) — raise your hands to your ears and say 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest). This marks the beginning of your prayer. 3) Qiyam (Standing) — stand upright with your hands crossed at chest level. Recite Surah Al-Fatiha and another Surah from the Quran. 4) Ruku (Bowing) — bow forward with your hands on your knees, keeping your back parallel to the ground. Say 'Subhana Rabbiyal Azeem' (Glory be to my Lord, the Greatest). 5) Qawmah (Rising) — rise from bowing to the standing position. Say 'Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah' (Allah hears those who praise Him). 6) Sujud (Prostration) — prostrate with your forehead, nose, hands, knees, and toes touching the ground. Say 'Subhana Rabbiyal A'la' (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High). 7) Tashahhud (Testimony) — sit between prostrations or at the end of prayer. Recite the testimony of faith and send blessings upon Prophet Muhammad.

Important Notes About Salah: Always face the Qibla (direction of the Kaaba in Mecca), maintain proper body covering (Satr): men from navel to below knees, women entire body except hands and face, perform Wudu before every prayer, pray at the prescribed times, and concentrate and be present during prayer (Khushu) for spiritual benefit.

THE 5 DAILY PRAYERS:
- Fajr (Dawn): Before sunrise. 2 Fard + 2 Sunnah = 4 total rak'ahs. The dawn prayer marks the beginning of the Islamic day and strengthens your faith.
- Dhuhr (Noon): After the sun passes its zenith. 4 Fard + 4 Sunnah Muakkadah + 2 Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah = 10 total rak'ahs. The longest prayer of the day helps find peace and clarity.
- Asr (Afternoon): Late afternoon before sunset. 4 Fard + 4 Sunnah Muakkadah + 2 Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah = 8 total rak'ahs. Seek Allah's pleasure in the late afternoon.
- Maghrib (Sunset): Just after the sun sets. 3 Fard + 2 Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah = 5 total rak'ahs. Unique among the five prayers with 3 Fard rak'ahs. Builds discipline and gratitude.
- Isha (Night): After nightfall. 4 Fard + 2 Sunnah Muakkadah + 2 Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah = 8 total rak'ahs. Connect with your Creator before sleep.

Total Daily: 17 Fard rak'ahs + 12 Sunnah Muakkadah = 29 combined total.
content.thinker:
How to Pray: A Complete Guide provides comprehensive instruction on Wudu (ablution), Salah (prayer), the five daily prayers, and the complete rak'ah breakdown.

WUDU (Ablution):
Wudu is the ritual purification that serves as both a physical cleansing and spiritual preparation for Salah. It is obligatory before every Fard (obligatory) prayer, Sunnah/Nafl (voluntary) prayers, and before touching the Quran. The eight steps follow a specific sequence established by the Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: 1) Niyyah — the internal intention, 2) Washing hands up to the wrists three times, 3) Rinsing the mouth thoroughly three times, 4) Inhaling water through the nose and expelling it three times, 5) Washing the entire face three times (from hairline to chin and ear to ear, including the beard for men), 6) Washing both arms up to and including the elbows three times, 7) Wiping the head once with wet hands, 8) Washing both feet up to and including the ankles three times. Each step has precise requirements: water must reach between fingers and toes, and all parts must be washed in the correct order. Wudu is invalidated by natural discharges, deep sleep, loss of consciousness, and touching one's private parts.

SALAH (Prayer) — The Seven Positions:
1) Niyyah (النية): The internal intention specifying which prayer is being performed. It must be clear and sincere. 2) Takbir (التكبير): The opening 'Allahu Akbar' when raising hands to the ears, marking the sacred boundary of prayer. 3) Qiyam (القيام): Standing position with hands folded at chest level (right hand over left), reciting Al-Fatiha followed by a second Surah. 4) Ruku (الركوع): Bowing with hands on knees, back parallel to ground, reciting 'Subhana Rabbiyal Azeem' (Glory be to my Lord, the Greatest) three times. 5) Qawmah (القومة): Rising from Ruku to standing with 'Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah, Rabbana lakal hamd' (Allah hears those who praise Him, our Lord, all praise is for You). 6) Sujud (السجود): Prostration with seven points of contact — forehead, nose, both hands, both knees, and toes — reciting 'Subhana Rabbiyal A'la' (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High) three times. Performed twice in each rak'ah. 7) Tashahhud (التشهد): Sitting position for the testimony of faith (At-Tahiyyatu lillahi was-salawatu wat-tayyibat), the Salawat (Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad), and the Du'a.

THE FIVE DAILY PRAYERS — Complete Breakdown:
- Fajr: 2 Fard + 2 Sunnah Muakkadah (before Fard) = 4 rak'ahs (before sunrise, approximately 4:30-5:30 AM)
- Dhuhr: 4 Sunnah Muakkadah (before Fard) + 4 Fard + 2 Sunnah Muakkadah (after Fard) + 2 Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah (after) = 10-12 rak'ahs (midday, approximately 12:00-1:00 PM)
- Asr: 4 Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah (before Fard) + 4 Fard = 4-8 rak'ahs (late afternoon, approximately 3:30-4:30 PM)
- Maghrib: 3 Fard + 2 Sunnah Muakkadah (after Fard) + 2 Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah (after) = 5-7 rak'ahs (after sunset, approximately 6:45-7:15 PM)
- Isha: 4 Fard + 2 Sunnah Muakkadah (after Fard) + 2 Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah (after) = 6-8 rak'ahs (after nightfall, approximately 8:15-9:30 PM)

RAK'AH BREAKDOWN TABLE:
| Prayer | Fard | Sunnah Muakkadah | Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah | Total |
| Fajr | 2 | 2 | 0 | 4 |
| Dhuhr | 4 | 4 | 2 | 10 |
| Asr | 4 | 0 | 2 | 6 |
| Maghrib | 3 | 0 | 2 | 5 |
| Isha | 4 | 2 | 2 | 8 |
| TOTAL | 17 | 8 | 8 | 33 |

Types of Prayers: Fard (Obligatory) — compulsory, missing them is a grave sin. Sunnah Muakkadah (Strongly Recommended) — highly emphasized, the Prophet ﷺ regularly performed them. Sunnah Ghair Muakkadah (Optional) — the Prophet ﷺ occasionally performed them, bringing extra reward.

Prayer is not merely physical movement — it demands Khushu (concentration and humility) and sincere connection with Allah. As Allah says: 'Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing' (Quran 29:45).

funFact: Did you know? The five daily prayers were prescribed during Prophet Muhammad's Night Journey (Isra and Mi'raj) to heaven. Originally, Allah commanded 50 prayers per day, but after several reductions through Prophet Musa's advice, it became 5 — yet the reward remains equal to 50!

quiz.q: When performing Wudu, which hand should you start with?

quiz.explanation: You say 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest) while raising your hands to your ears to begin Salah. This marks the beginning of your prayer.

quiz.q: How many Fard rak'ahs are there in total across all 5 daily prayers?
quiz.explanation: There are 17 Fard rak'ahs in total: Fajr (2), Dhuhr (4), Asr (4), Maghrib (3), and Isha (4).

quiz.q: Which prayer has 3 Fard rak'ahs?
quiz.explanation: Maghrib (sunset prayer) is unique as it has 3 Fard rak'ahs, while all other prayers have either 2 or 4 Fard rak'ahs.

quiz.q: What is Sujud in Salah?
quiz.explanation: Sujud is the prostration position where your forehead, nose, hands, knees, and toes touch the ground. It is performed twice in each rak'ah, and you say 'Subhana Rabbiyal A'la.'

title: Honesty

content.starter: Honesty means always telling the truth! Allah loves people who are honest. Even if telling the truth is hard, it's always the right thing to do. When we're honest, people trust us and Allah is pleased with us!
content.explorer: Honesty (Sidq) is one of the most important values in Islam. The Prophet ﷺ was known as 'Al-Amin' — the Trustworthy — because he always told the truth. Islam teaches us to be honest in our words, actions, and intentions. Lying is a major sin that can damage relationships and break trust. Being honest, even when it's difficult, earns Allah's love and the respect of others.
content.thinker: Honesty (Sidq) and trustworthiness (Amanah) are foundational Islamic virtues. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.' Honesty is not merely about not lying — it encompasses sincerity in intentions, accuracy in reporting, and integrity in all dealings. Allah says in the Quran: 'O you who believe, fear Allah and be among the truthful' (Surah At-Tawbah 9:119). The concept extends to being honest with oneself, honest in worship, and honest in business dealings.

funFact: Did you know? Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was called 'Al-Amin' (The Trustworthy) even before he became a prophet — because he NEVER told a lie!

quiz.q: What was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ's nickname before prophethood?
quiz.explanation: He was called 'Al-Amin' (The Trustworthy) because he always told the truth.

quiz.q: Is honesty only about not lying?
options: No, it includes sincerity and integrity too
quiz.explanation: Honesty includes being truthful, sincere, and having integrity in everything.

quiz.q: What does Allah say about truthful people?
quiz.explanation: Allah loves truthful people and promises them Paradise.

title: Kindness

content.starter: Kindness means being nice to everyone! Help your friends, smile at people, share your toys, and be gentle. The Prophet ﷺ was the kindest person ever! When we're kind, Allah rewards us and everyone loves us!
content.explorer: Kindness (Ihsan) is at the heart of Islamic teaching. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The most beloved of people to Allah are those who are most beneficial to people.' Being kind means helping others, smiling, sharing, and treating everyone with respect — whether they're Muslim or not. Islam teaches that even a smile is charity (sadaqah).
content.thinker: Kindness (Ihsan and Rahmah) is a comprehensive Islamic virtue. The Prophet ﷺ embodied mercy — the Quran describes him as 'a mercy to all the worlds' (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:107). Kindness extends to all creation: family, neighbors, strangers, animals, and even the environment. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Charity does not decrease wealth. No one forgives another except that Allah increases his honor. And no one humbles himself for the sake of Allah except that Allah raises his status.' True kindness in Islam is not performative but stems from genuine love for Allah and His creation.

funFact: Did you know? The Prophet ﷺ said that even smiling at someone is a form of charity! You can earn rewards just by being friendly!

quiz.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about smiling?
quiz.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ said even a smile is charity (sadaqah).

quiz.q: Who should we be kind to?
quiz.explanation: Islam teaches us to be kind to everyone — Muslim or not.

quiz.q: What is the most beloved person to Allah?
quiz.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ said the most beloved to Allah are those most beneficial to people.

title: Respect

content.starter: Respect means treating people nicely and politely! We respect our parents, teachers, and elders. We say 'please' and 'thank you.' We listen when others talk. Allah loves people who are respectful!
content.explorer: Respect (Adab) is a key Islamic value. The Quran commands us to honor our parents, be kind to neighbors, and treat elders with dignity. The Prophet ﷺ taught that respect is not just about words but actions — standing up for elders, listening attentively, and honoring others' feelings. Respect also extends to respecting differences of opinion.
content.thinker: Respect (Adab) in Islam is a comprehensive concept that encompasses how we relate to Allah, His creation, and ourselves. The Quran says: 'And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be dutiful to your parents' (Surah Al-Isra 17:23). Respect for parents is given such high status that it appears immediately after the command to worship Allah alone. Beyond parents, Islam teaches respect for scholars, neighbors, the elderly, and even strangers. The Prophet ﷺ demonstrated this by standing when a funeral passed, greeting children, and honoring the rights of neighbors regardless of their faith.

funFact: Did you know? In Islam, respecting your parents is considered the SECOND most important duty after worshipping Allah alone!

quiz.q: What comes right after worshipping Allah in importance?
quiz.explanation: The Quran commands us to worship Allah alone, then to honor our parents.

quiz.q: How should we treat elders?
quiz.explanation: Islam teaches us to treat elders with honor and dignity.

quiz.q: What does 'Adab' mean?
quiz.explanation: Adab means respect, good manners, and proper etiquette in Islam.

title: Patience

content.starter: Patience means waiting calmly and not getting upset when things are hard! When you're sick, or something goes wrong, or you have to wait — be patient! Allah loves patient people and will reward them!
content.explorer: Patience (Sabr) is one of the greatest virtues in Islam. The Quran says: 'Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account' (Surah Az-Zumar 39:10). Sabr means staying calm during difficulties, resisting temptation, and being content with Allah's plan. The Prophet ﷺ compared patience to a precious gem — it's hard to find but incredibly valuable.
content.thinker: Patience (Sabr) is one of the most emphasized virtues in Islam. The Quran mentions it over 70 times. Sabr has three dimensions: patience in obeying Allah (perseverance), patience in avoiding sin (restraint), and patience during hardship (endurance). Allah says: 'And be patient, for indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good' (Surah Hud 11:115). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'How wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all his affairs are good, and this does not apply to anyone except the believer. If something good happens to him, he is grateful, and that is good for him. If something bad happens to him, he bears it with patience, and that is good for him.'

funFact: Did you know? Allah mentions patience (Sabr) over 70 times in the Quran — it's one of the most important qualities a Muslim can have!

quiz.q: What is 'Sabr'?
quiz.explanation: Sabr means patience — staying calm during difficulties and trusting Allah.

quiz.q: How many times does Allah mention patience in the Quran?
quiz.explanation: Allah mentions patience (Sabr) over 70 times in the Quran.

quiz.q: What happens to patient people?
quiz.explanation: Allah says the patient will be given their reward without account.

title: Gratitude

content.starter: Gratitude means saying 'thank you' to Allah for everything! For food, family, friends, health — everything! When we're thankful, Allah gives us more blessings. A grateful heart is a happy heart!
content.explorer: Gratitude (Shukr) means recognizing and appreciating Allah's blessings. The Quran says: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you' (Surah Ibrahim 14:7). Gratitude isn't just saying 'Alhamdulillah' — it's using Allah's blessings in ways that please Him. When we're grateful for health, we use it to do good. When we're grateful for wealth, we share it with others.
content.thinker: Gratitude (Shukr) is a comprehensive Islamic concept that goes beyond simple thankfulness. It has three dimensions: gratitude of the heart (recognizing blessings), gratitude of the tongue (verbal thanks and praise), and gratitude of the limbs (using blessings in obedience to Allah). The Quran warns against ingratitude: 'If you are ungrateful, indeed, my punishment is severe' (Surah Ibrahim 14:7). The Prophet ﷺ would pray at night until his feet would swell, and when asked why, he would say: 'Should I not be a grateful servant?' Gratitude transforms our perspective — even in hardship, a grateful person finds blessings to thank Allah for.

funFact: Did you know? The Prophet ﷺ would pray at night until his feet swelled — and when asked why, he said: 'Should I not be a grateful servant?'

quiz.q: What does 'Shukr' mean?
quiz.explanation: Shukr means gratitude — being thankful to Allah for His blessings.

quiz.q: What does Allah promise to grateful people?
quiz.explanation: Allah says: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.'

quiz.q: What are the three dimensions of gratitude?
quiz.explanation: Gratitude is expressed through the heart (recognizing), tongue (thanking), and limbs (using blessings to do good).

title: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

content.starter: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was the best person ever! He was kind, honest, and brave. He taught us about Allah and how to be good Muslims. He loved children and animals. We follow his example every day!
content.explorer: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in Mecca in 570 CE. He was known as 'Al-Amin' (The Trustworthy) even before prophethood. At age 40, Angel Jibril brought him the first revelation in the cave of Hira. He spent 23 years teaching Islam, facing persecution, and building a just community. He passed away in Medina in 632 CE, leaving behind a message for all of humanity.
content.thinker: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the final messenger of Allah and the most influential person in history. Born an orphan, raised by his grandfather Abdul Muttalib and then his uncle Abu Talib, he grew up to be known for his truthfulness and integrity. The Quran describes him as 'a mercy to all the worlds' (21:107). His life (Seerah) is a comprehensive guide — from the early persecution in Mecca to the establishment of the first Islamic state in Medina, from the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah to the conquest of Mecca. He taught through example: he prayed until his feet swelled, gave charity until he had nothing left, and treated everyone with dignity regardless of their status.

funFact: Did you know? Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was an orphan — his father died before he was born and his mother when he was only 6 years old. Despite this, he became the greatest person in history!

quiz.q: In which city was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ born?
quiz.explanation: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in Mecca in 570 CE.

quiz.q: What was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ's nickname before prophethood?
quiz.explanation: He was called 'Al-Amin' (The Trustworthy) because he always told the truth.

quiz.q: How old was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ when he received the first revelation?
quiz.explanation: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was 40 years old when Angel Jibril brought the first revelation.

title: Prophet Ibrahim

content.starter: Prophet Ibrahim loved Allah more than anything! He looked at the stars and knew they couldn't be God. He broke the idols people worshipped and told them only Allah deserves worship. Allah made him a great leader!
content.explorer: Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) is one of the greatest prophets. He realized at a young age that idols couldn't be God — they couldn't create or help anyone. He broke the idols and called people to worship Allah alone. Allah tested him greatly — He asked Ibrahim to leave his homeland, sacrifice his son, and build the Kaaba. Ibrahim obeyed every command, showing incredible faith.
content.thinker: Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) is known as 'Khalilullah' — the Friend of Allah. His story is one of absolute submission to divine will. He questioned his father's idol worship, challenged King Namrud, and was thrown into fire for his faith — yet Allah saved him. The sacrifice of his son Ismail (Ismail) is commemorated every year during Eid al-Adha. Ibrahim's willingness to leave his wife Hajar and infant son Ismail in the desert of Mecca — trusting completely in Allah's plan — led to the establishment of the Kaaba and the Zamzam well. He is the patriarch of the Abrahamic faiths and an enduring example of total trust in Allah.

funFact: Did you know? When Ibrahim was thrown into a giant fire, Allah said 'O fire, be cool and peaceful!' — and the fire didn't even burn him!

quiz.q: What was Prophet Ibrahim known as?
quiz.explanation: Ibrahim is called 'Khalilullah' — the Friend of Allah.

quiz.q: What did Ibrahim break?
quiz.explanation: Ibrahim broke the idols people were worshipping to show only Allah deserves worship.

quiz.q: What did Allah ask Ibrahim to build?
quiz.explanation: Allah asked Ibrahim to build the Kaaba in Mecca.

title: Islamic Civilization

content.starter: Muslims built amazing things long ago! They made beautiful mosques, hospitals, schools, and libraries. They studied science, math, and medicine. Muslims invented things we still use today — like cameras, universities, and coffee!
content.explorer: Islamic civilization made incredible contributions to the world. Muslim scholars invented algebra, developed modern medicine, built the first universities, and preserved ancient Greek knowledge. Cities like Baghdad, Cordoba, and Cairo were centers of learning. Inventions include the camera (camera obscura), surgical instruments, and windmills. Muslims also built beautiful architecture like the Alhambra and the Dome of the Rock.
content.thinker: The Islamic Golden Age (8th-14th centuries) was one of the most productive periods of scholarship in human history. Scholars like Al-Khwarizmi (algebra), Ibn Sina (medicine), Al-Kindi (philosophy), and Fatima al-Fihri (first university) transformed human knowledge. The House of Wisdom in Baghdad translated and preserved Greek, Persian, and Indian texts that would have been lost. Islamic civilization pioneered hospitals (bimaristans), observatories, and public libraries. The concept of the university was literally invented by Muslims — the University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco, founded by Fatima al-Fihri in 859 CE, is recognized by UNESCO as the oldest existing university.

funFact: Did you know? The first university in the world was built by a Muslim woman — Fatima al-Fihri — in Morocco in the year 859 CE!

quiz.q: What did Al-Khwarizmi invent?
quiz.explanation: Al-Khwarizmi invented algebra — the word 'algorithm' comes from his name!

quiz.q: Who built the first university in the world?
quiz.explanation: Fatima al-Fihri, a Muslim woman, built the first university in Morocco in 859 CE.

quiz.q: What was the Islamic Golden Age known for?
options: Advances in science, math, and medicine
quiz.explanation: Muslims made incredible advances in science, math, medicine, and many other fields.

title: Ramadan

content.starter: Ramadan is the best month! It's when Allah sent the Quran. We fast from sunrise to sunset — no eating or drinking! At night, we pray, read Quran, and have iftar with family. Everyone is happy and kind during Ramadan!
content.explorer: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar and the holiest month for Muslims. The Quran was first revealed during Ramadan. Muslims fast from dawn to sunset, refraining from food, drink, and other physical needs. It's a time of increased prayer, charity, and Quran reading. Ramadan teaches self-discipline, empathy for the poor, and brings families and communities together.
content.thinker: Ramadan is the month in which the Quran was revealed as guidance for humanity (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185). Fasting (Sawm) during Ramadan is the fourth pillar of Islam and serves multiple purposes: developing taqwa (God-consciousness), purifying the soul, building empathy for the less fortunate, and strengthening community bonds. The pre-dawn meal (Suhoor) and sunset meal (Iftar) create a spiritual rhythm throughout the month. The last 10 nights are especially sacred, as Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Power) — described as 'better than a thousand months' — falls within them. Ramadan transforms communities: charity increases, tempers cool, and hearts soften.

funFact: Did you know? Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Power) in Ramadan is better than 1,000 months — that's over 83 years of blessings in just one night!

quiz.q: During which month was the Quran revealed?
quiz.explanation: The Quran was first revealed during the month of Ramadan.

quiz.q: What is Laylat al-Qadr?
options: The Night of Power, better than 1,000 months
quiz.explanation: Laylat al-Qadr (Night of Power) is better than 1,000 months of worship.

quiz.q: What is the pre-dawn meal called?
quiz.explanation: The pre-dawn meal before fasting is called Suhoor.

title: Eid al-Fitr

content.starter: Eid al-Fitr is the happy day after Ramadan! We wear new clothes, eat yummy food, give gifts, and say 'Eid Mubarak!' to everyone. We give money to poor people called Zakat al-Fitr. It's like a big party for Allah!
content.explorer: Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan and is one of the two major Islamic holidays. Muslims gather for a special prayer, give Zakat al-Fitr (charity to the poor), wear their best clothes, and celebrate with family and friends. Children receive gifts and money (Eidi). It's a day of joy, gratitude, and community after a month of fasting and worship.
content.thinker: Eid al-Fitr ('Festival of Breaking the Fast') is celebrated on the first day of Shawwal, the month following Ramadan. It begins with a special congregational prayer and sermon, followed by Zakat al-Fitr — a mandatory charity given before the Eid prayer to ensure even the poorest can celebrate. The Prophet ﷺ would wear his best clothes on Eid and apply perfume. Eid is a day of celebration, but also of reflection — thanking Allah for the strength to complete Ramadan and asking for acceptance of our worship. It strengthens community bonds as Muslims visit relatives, share meals, and reconcile differences.

funFact: Did you know? On Eid, you must give charity (Zakat al-Fitr) BEFORE the Eid prayer — so even poor people can celebrate!

quiz.q: When is Eid al-Fitr celebrated?
quiz.explanation: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated at the end of Ramadan.

quiz.q: What must Muslims give before Eid prayer?
quiz.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is charity given before Eid prayer so the poor can celebrate too.

quiz.q: What do we say to others on Eid?
quiz.explanation: We say 'Eid Mubarak' — meaning 'Blessed Eid!'

title: Eid al-Adha

content.starter: Eid al-Adha is the big Eid! It remembers when Prophet Ibrahim was ready to sacrifice his son for Allah. Allah was so happy with his faith that He sent a sheep instead! We sacrifice an animal and share the meat with family and poor people!
content.explorer: Eid al-Adha ('Festival of Sacrifice') honors Prophet Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son Ismail for Allah. Before Eid, Muslims who can afford it sacrifice an animal (sheep, goat, cow, or camel) and divide the meat into three parts: one for family, one for friends and neighbors, one for the poor. It coincides with the Hajj pilgrimage and is one of the two major Islamic holidays.
content.thinker: Eid al-Adha commemorates one of the most profound acts of faith in Islamic history — Prophet Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son Ismail in complete obedience to Allah. Just as Ibrahim was about to carry out the sacrifice, Allah replaced Ismail with a ram, and the sacrifice was accepted symbolically. This event is commemorated by millions of Muslims worldwide who sacrifice an animal during the days of Eid. The meat is divided into thirds: family, friends/neighbors, and the poor. Eid al-Adha coincides with the Hajj pilgrimage — while pilgrims are at Arafat, Muslims worldwide celebrate this festival of sacrifice, gratitude, and community.

funFact: Did you know? Eid al-Adha remembers when Prophet Ibrahim was ready to sacrifice his son for Allah — but Allah sent a ram instead as a test of faith!

quiz.q: What does Eid al-Adha remember?
options: Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son
quiz.explanation: Eid al-Adha remembers when Prophet Ibrahim was ready to sacrifice his son for Allah.

quiz.q: How many parts is the sacrificial meat divided into?
quiz.explanation: The meat is divided into three: family, friends/neighbors, and the poor.

quiz.q: What did Allah send instead of Ibrahim's son?
quiz.explanation: Allah sent a ram to be sacrificed instead, accepting Ibrahim's willingness.

title: Al-Khwarizmi - Father of Algebra

content.starter: Al-Khwarizmi was a great Muslim math genius who lived a long time ago. He invented Algebra, which helps us solve math problems using letters and numbers! He also showed the whole world how to use the number zero and introduced the numbers 1 to 9, which we still use today!
content.explorer: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi (c. 780–850 CE) was a legendary mathematician, astronomer, and geographer who worked in Baghdad's House of Wisdom. He wrote a revolutionary book called 'Kitab al-Jabr' from which we get the word 'Algebra'. He also popularised the Hindu-Arabic numeral system, including the decimal point and the number zero, in the Islamic world and Europe, establishing the foundation of modern mathematics.
content.thinker: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi (c. 780–850 CE) is widely regarded as the Father of Algebra. Working at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad during the Islamic Golden Age, his masterpiece, 'The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing' ('Al-Kitab al-mukhtasar fi hisab al-jabr wal-muqabala'), formalized a systematic way of solving linear and quadratic equations. He introduced the Arabic numeral system to the West, and his latinized name eventually gave rise to the term 'algorithm', celebrating his lasting legacy as a pioneer of mathematics and computer science.

funFact: Did you know? The word 'algebra' comes from the title of his book 'Al-Jabr' (meaning restoring/completion), and the word 'algorithm' is a translation of his own name, Al-Khwarizmi!

quiz.q: What branch of mathematics did Al-Khwarizmi invent?
quiz.explanation: Al-Khwarizmi wrote 'Al-Jabr', creating a structured system for solving equations called algebra.

quiz.q: Where did Al-Khwarizmi carry out his scientific research?
options: The House of Wisdom in Baghdad
quiz.explanation: The House of Wisdom in Baghdad was the premier intellectual hub of the Islamic Golden Age.

quiz.q: Which modern computer science term is derived from Al-Khwarizmi's name?
quiz.explanation: The word 'algorithm' comes from the Latin translation of his name, 'Algoritmi'.

title: Ibn Sina - Father of Medicine

content.starter: Ibn Sina, also known as Avicenna, was a super-smart doctor and philosopher! He wrote a massive medical encyclopedia called 'The Canon of Medicine'. It was so comprehensive that universities in Europe used it for hundreds of years to teach people how to become doctors!
content.explorer: Ibn Sina (Avicenna, 980–1037 CE) was an extraordinary Persian polymath who is celebrated as one of the most significant thinkers of the Islamic Golden Age. He memorized the entire Quran by age 10 and was a practicing doctor by age 18. His world-famous book, 'The Canon of Medicine' ('Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb'), became the standard medical textbook across Europe and Asia for over 600 years.
content.thinker: Ibn Sina (Avicenna, 980–1037 CE) was a legendary scholar whose contributions shaped early medical science and medieval philosophy. His massive compilation 'The Canon of Medicine' introduced revolutionary ideas, including quarantine to contain infectious diseases, clinical trials, and pharmacology. In addition to medicine, his encyclopedia 'The Book of Healing' ('Kitab al-Shifa') covered logic, natural sciences, and metaphysics, blending Islamic theology with rational philosophy.

funFact: Did you know? Ibn Sina was so brilliant that he memorized the entire Quran by the age of 10 and became a respected, practicing physician at just 18 years old!

quiz.q: What is the name of Ibn Sina's famous medical textbook?
quiz.explanation: Ibn Sina wrote 'The Canon of Medicine', which remained the standard text for centuries.

quiz.q: At what age did Ibn Sina memorize the entire Quran?
quiz.explanation: Ibn Sina memorized the Quran at age 10, displaying genius intellect from a very young age.

quiz.q: Which medical practice did Ibn Sina pioneer to control the spread of contagious diseases?
quiz.explanation: Ibn Sina hypothesized that diseases spread through microscopic particles and pioneered quarantine methods.

title: Al-Razi - Pioneer of Chemistry

content.starter: Al-Razi was a kind-hearted doctor and an amazing chemist. He was the first to realize that clean hospital rooms help sick people heal faster, and he designed advanced laboratory tools to study chemicals!
content.explorer: Al-Razi (Rhazes, 854–925 CE) was an outstanding clinical doctor and chemist. He was the first to differentiate between smallpox and measles, writing a medical treatise on them. In chemistry, he of categorized chemical substances for the first time and designed lab equipment, including retorts and glass flasks, which chemists still use to run experiments.
content.thinker: Abu Bakr al-Razi (Rhazes, 854–925 CE) was a titan of clinical medicine, experimental science, and chemistry. As head of the main hospital in Baghdad, he selected its building site by hanging raw meat in various locations to find the place with the cleanest air. In his masterwork 'Kitab al-Hawi' (The Comprehensive Book), he recorded clinical case studies. In chemistry, his taxonomy of minerals and chemical compounds laid the framework for contemporary chemistry.

funFact: Did you know? In his chemistry lab, Al-Razi invented kerosene lamps and categorized chemical elements. In medicine, he chose hospital locations by hanging raw meat around Baghdad to find where air was cleanest!

quiz.q: How did Al-Razi choose the cleanest place to build Baghdad's hospital?
options: By hanging raw meat to see where it decayed slowest
quiz.explanation: He hung meat around the city; the location where the meat stayed fresh longest had the cleanest air.

quiz.q: Al-Razi was the first physician in history to distinguish between which two diseases?
quiz.explanation: His treatise on smallpox and measles was acclaimed internationally and translated into multiple languages.

quiz.q: What did Al-Razi classify in his chemical studies?
quiz.explanation: He created an early classification system for minerals and organic substances, laying foundations for chemistry.

title: Al-Biruni - Master of Sciences

content.starter: Al-Biruni was a globetrotting science detective. He loved mapping the Earth and looking at the stars! Using a mountain and simple mathematics, he calculated how big the Earth is, and got it almost perfectly correct!
content.explorer: Al-Biruni (973–1048 CE) was a natural scientist and geographer. He was fluent in multiple languages, including Sanskrit, Persian, Arabic, and Greek. He pioneered geodesy, using trigonometric math to calculate the radius and circumference of the Earth with less than 1% error. He also wrote about the mineral composition of gems and documented ancient calendar systems.
content.thinker: Abu al-Rayhan al-Biruni (973–1048 CE) is celebrated as one of the greatest scientists of all time. He excelled in astronomy, geodesy, sociology, and mineralogy. He designed unique mathematical equations using the height of a mountain in modern Pakistan to calculate the radius of the Earth, centuries before satellite observations. His scholarship on India ('Kitab al-Hind') is considered the first objective ethnography and comparative religion study.

funFact: Did you know? Using trigonometry and a single mountain, Al-Biruni calculated the size of the Earth with 99.6% accuracy, a calculation that is nearly identical to modern satellites!

quiz.q: What geographic measurement did Al-Biruni calculate with incredible precision?
quiz.explanation: Using a mountain and trigonometric formulas, Al-Biruni calculated the radius of the Earth with under 1% error.

quiz.q: Al-Biruni wrote 'Kitab al-Hind' after studying the culture and sciences of which region?
quiz.explanation: He traveled extensively in India, learning Sanskrit and writing a comprehensive cultural analysis.

quiz.q: Which astronomical instrument did Al-Biruni develop further for navigation?
quiz.explanation: Al-Biruni designed astronomical maps and improved astrolabes to calculate solar positions and prayer directions.

title: Al-Ghazali - Islamic Philosophy

content.starter: Al-Ghazali was a wise teacher who studied how people think. He taught that having a clean, kind heart is just as important as being super smart, and he helped people find peace of mind!
content.explorer: Al-Ghazali (1058–1111 CE) was one of the most influential Islamic theologians and philosophers. Known as 'Hujjat al-Islam' (Proof of Islam), he taught at Nizamiyya, the grandest academy of his time. He wrote beautiful books that combined intellectual study with spiritual reflection, helping people balance rational science with positive spiritual morals.
content.thinker: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (1058–1111 CE) profoundly shaped Islamic philosophy, theology, and Sufism. In his major work, 'The Incoherence of the Philosophers' ('Tahafut al-Falasifah'), he debated Greek metaphysics. However, in his masterpiece 'Ihya Ulum al-Din' (The Revival of the Religious Sciences), he synthesized jurisprudence, intellectual theology, and spiritual mysticism, establishing character-building and ethics as the heart of scientific and personal pursuits.

funFact: Did you know? Al-Ghazali's title is 'Hujjat al-Islam' (Proof of Islam) due to his incredible depth of knowledge. He believed the ultimate goal of learning is to build noble character and inner peace!

quiz.q: What title is Al-Ghazali famously known as?
quiz.explanation: He is renowned as 'Hujjat al-Islam' due to his mastery over theological philosophy.

quiz.q: What has Al-Ghazali described as the revival of religious sciences in his masterpiece?
options: Ethics, spirituality, and knowledge of the heart
quiz.explanation: 'Ihya Ulum al-Din' focuses on rejuvenating faith, moral character, and spiritual consciousness.

quiz.q: According to Al-Ghazali, the objective of obtaining knowledge is:
options: To build noble character and get closer to Allah
quiz.explanation: He taught that intellectual knowledge is worthless unless accompanied by spiritual humility and high ethical standards.

title: Fatima al-Fihri - First University

content.starter: Fatima al-Fihri was a wealthy and generous Muslim woman who moved to Morocco. She loved reading, science, and education so much that she used her entire inheritance to build the University of al-Qarawiyyin, the oldest university in the world!
content.explorer: Fatima al-Fihri (800–880 CE) was an inspirational educator and philanthropist. In 859 CE, she founded the University and Mosque of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco. UNESCO and the Guinness World Records recognize it as the oldest continuously operating, degree-granting educational institution in the world.
content.thinker: Fatima al-Fihri (800–880 CE) is a pioneer in global higher education. After migrating to Fez and inheriting a vast fortune, she vowed to spend her wealth in service of her community. She oversaw the complex architecture and construction of the Al-Qarawiyyin mosque and university complex, fasting daily during its multi-year construction. The university became a hub of world education, hosting Christian, Jewish, and Muslim scholars like Pope Sylvester II.

funFact: Did you know? Fatima al-Fihri built the University of al-Qarawiyyin in 859 CE. It is officially certified by UNESCO as the oldest running university in human history!

quiz.q: In which city and country did Fatima al-Fihri found the oldest university?
quiz.explanation: She founded the University of al-Qarawiyyin in the city of Fez, Morocco.

quiz.q: What did Fatima do during the construction of Al-Qarawiyyin?
options: She fasted daily until its completion
She went on a sailing trip
quiz.explanation: As an act of piety, Fatima al-Fihri vowed to fast every single day during the years it took to build.

quiz.q: According to UNESCO, what distinction does the University of al-Qarawiyyin hold?
options: Oldest continuously operating, degree-granting university in the world
quiz.explanation: Al-Qarawiyyin has been fully operating and granting college degrees continuously since 859 CE.

title: Ibn Khaldun - Father of Sociology

content.starter: Ibn Khaldun was an expert storyteller and historian. He was the first scholar to realize that studying *groups of people* and how societies grow is a special science, which we now call sociology!
content.explorer: Ibn Khaldun (1332–1406 CE) was a legendary Arab historian, sociologist, and philosopher. In his amazing book, 'Al-Muqaddimah' (The Introduction), he introduced 'Asabiyyah' (social cohesion), explaining how great empires rise, thrive, grow old, and eventually dissolve.
content.thinker: Ibn Khaldun (1332–1406 CE) is widely regarded as a founding father of sociology, economics, history, and demography. His monumental book 'Al-Muqaddimah' formulated a philosophy of history. He introduced the concept of 'Asabiyyah' — social cohesion or group solidarity — to explain historical cycles, analyzing how nomadic cultures establish civilizations which rise, decay after three generations, and yield to new dynamic social alliances.

funFact: Did you know? Ibn Khaldun wrote his entire world-changing book 'Al-Muqaddimah' (representing early sociology and economics) years before Western scholars established sociology as a field!

quiz.q: What is the title of Ibn Khaldun's world-famous historical introduction book?
quiz.explanation: He wrote 'Al-Muqaddimah', which analyzed the sociopolitical growth of societies.

quiz.q: Which major scientific discipline did Ibn Khaldun pioneer centuries before Western scholars?
quiz.explanation: His systematic analysis of social patterns and historical cycles makes him the father of sociology.

quiz.q: What is 'Asabiyyah', the core concept proposed by Ibn Khaldun?
quiz.explanation: 'Asabiyyah' is the community bond or social group solidarity that enables societies to build stable nations.
